why_this_rate: Part of the candidate rather than a constant, because it is one of the two things this comparison is for. An all-pass cascade keeps its notches at fixed ratios in the tangent of frequency, so the rate decides how far up the band those ratios start to close -- and the profile is read to sixteen kilohertz, which is where a chain running at thirty-two has nothing left.

map.why: One corner per setting the run asked, fitted from that setting's own notches. A readout and not a law: what is claimed is the section count and the rate, which a table with a free entry per setting cannot arrange, and the corner's own figure is this reading's rounding error.

The run held the type's mix at the top of its range, so the cascade is summed with the dry at equal weight. How deep that makes a notch is decided by the band reading rather than here: a band a twelfth of an octave wide reports the energy across a notch, not the null.
